Subject (in full) The Naval Academy of the Republic of China

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

Commr of Police
Sir:
Information
R. E. Yorke
D. C. (Sp. Br.)

With reference to the remarks of the
Commissioner of Police (attached), discreet enquiries
have been conducted and it was ascertained that
the "Naval Academy of the Republic of China",
located at the former site of the Naval Hospital,
Koochongmiao, Nantao, is the only institute
established by the "New Central Government" for
naval training purposes. The school does not
employ German instructors and has no branch schools
in the Woosung area or elsewhere.

Enquiries in German circles also fail to
disclose any such engagements.

C. Crawford
D. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT

Subject The Naval Academy of the Republic of China - school-opening
ceremony held.

Made by. D.S.I. Tan Iien Tih Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford.

(Vide Special
Branch report
of 13/4/40.)

The Naval Academy of the Republic of China,
(Wang Ching Wei sponsored) which is located on the
former site of the Naval Hospital, Kaochongmiao, Nantao,
held a formal opening ceremony on the premises of the
school at 10 a.m. May 11, 1940. This academy commenced the
enlistment of cadets for the second term in April, 1940
and expected the enrolment of 500 cadets, but only 137
candidates were enrolled.

During the ceremony, speeches appropriate to
the occasion were made by Mr. Chiang Hsi Yuen (姜西園),
principal, and Ling Hsiao (凌霄), representative of
Mr. Wang Ching Wei and Vice Minister of the Navy in the
"New Central Government." The ceremony concluded at
11.30 a.m.

Commr of Police
Sir:
Information
R. G. Forbes
D. C. (7. 3-5)

Subject. The Naval Academy of the Republic of China (中華民國海軍學校).

Made by. D. I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford

(Vide Special
Branch report
dated 13/5/39).

With reference to the attached extract of
the North China Daily News, dated April 9, 1940,
regarding a notice inserted by the "Central Naval
Academy of the Republic of China", enquiries have
ascertained that the school in question first came
into existence in April, 1939, under the auspices
of the late "Reformed Government". It was then
known as the "Pacification River Police School" with
school premises on the former site of the Naval
Hospital, Kaochongmiao, Nantao. However, following
the inauguration of the "New Central Government"
in Nanking, on March 30, 1940, the school was taken
over by the latter government and has since been
renamed as "The Naval Academy of the Republic of
China".

The intention is, at present, to enlist
500 new cadets and classes are scheduled to
commence in May, 1940.

One copy of the regulations of the school,
application form and pledge form, has been obtained
and is attached hereto together with translation.

Pan Lien Pih

APR 8 1940

THE
CENTRAL NAVAL ACADEMY
OF THE REPUBLIC
OF CHINA

ENTRANCE EXAMINATION
FOR NEW CADETS

Notice is hereby given that the second annual entrance examination for new cadets will be held on April 18 and 19. Apart from oral and physical examinations, Chinese literature, history and geography of East Asia, mathematics (arithmetic, geometry, algebra), physics, and foreign languages (Japanese or English) are the other subjects on which written examinations will be given. Those who wish to take the examination must be graduates of junior middle-school or those who have received education of same standard. The ages are between 17 and 22.

Cadets will be trained for two years. During the training period they will be paid $12 monthly and furnished living quarters with board. After graduation cadets will be sent on board training ships as midshipmen, drawing a monthly salary of $60. After six months or one year, they will be appointed by the Government as ensigns of the new navy that lead to the highest rank of admirals. It is also a scheme of the school that prominent cadets of good character and talent be sent to Japanese Naval School for advanced study, at Government expense.

The registration for the above will be closed on April 17. Volunteers are requested to register their names as soon as possible. Particulars and forms of registration will be supplied on application.

PACIFICATION RIVER POLICE SCHOOL
- ENLISTMENT OF CADETS
-----

The following are the rules and regulations
governing the enlistment of 1st and second class cadets
for the "Pacification River Police School" (靖水巡學校)
recently established by the "Reformed Government" :-

(1) Date of the opening of the school : June 1.

(2) Qualifications of applicants :-

| Class | Education | Age | No. to be enlisted |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1st | Graduates from junior middle schools. | Between 16 & 25. | 45 |
| 2nd | Graduates from junior primary schools. | Between 16 & 25. | 200 |

(3) Place of Examination : Nanking, Shanghai, Soochow,
Hangchow, Yangchow and Pengpu.

(4) Applications for enrolment are to be made to the
following places :-

Pacification Department of "Reformed Government."

Offices of this school (former site of Nantao
Naval Hospital) at 20 North Szechuen-
Li, North Szechuen Road.

Pacification Commander's Headquarters for the
Second Area at Soochow.

Pacification Commander's Headquarters for the
1st Area at Hangchow.

Pacification Commander's Headquarters for the
5th Area at Yangchow.

Anhwei Office of the Pacification Forces at Pengpu.

(5) Date of Examination :

May 20 - Physical and verbal tests.

May 21 - Chinese language, mathematics, science,
Oriental History, Geography.

- 2 -

(6) Date for applying : To apply before May 19.
(7) Period in school : Two years for 1st class cadets
and 6 months for 2nd class cadets.
(8) Treatment in school: A 1st class cadet while in
school will receive an allowance
of $12 per month and a 2nd class
cadet will receive $6 per month.
The school will supply food,
lodging, clothing and bedding.
(9) Treatment after graduation :
1st class cadets, after graduation
will be appointed officers of
river police at $45 per month and
2nd class cadets will be appointed
junior officers and privates at
from $15 to $20.
(10) Duties of river police :
To undertake precautionary service
on waterways with Nanking and
Shanghai as the headquarters.

Subject. Pamphlets dropped from an airplane on the morning of May 13, 1939.
Made by. and Forwarded by. J.I. Crawford

During the morning of May 13, 1939, copies
of a pamphlet containing an advertisement enlisting
cadets for a "Pacification River Police School"
(绥靖水巡学校) to be established by the "Reformed
Government", were dropped and fell in the Settlement
from a seaplane. According to this pamphlet, 40
first class cadets and 200 second class cadets
will be enrolled and will, after graduation, be
attached to the river police as junior officers
and privates for undertaking precautionary service
on waterways. Applicants in Shanghai are required
to attend the offices of the School at 20 North
Szechuen Road Alleyway, North Szechuen Road, while the
school, which will begin classes on June 1, 1939,
will be established on the former site of the naval
hospital at Kaochongmiao, Antao.
A translation of this pamphlet is attached.

C. Crawford
